claimed_outcome:
Decision: complete_for_decision, but fail closed. Do not replace the authoritative wake transport with `codex resume SESSION_ID MESSAGE`.

Key findings:

- Installed package is `@openai/codex` 0.151.0, Apache-2.0. Native binary SHA-256: `9739cbc928b9c573be83256acd46668f5dd4f119d2d09e05246895ca2aaf0c9a`.
- Exact source is tag `rust-v0.151.0`, commit `78c290807ce710180111df227df3b7a4fe845452`. [Release](https://github.com/openai/codex/releases/tag/rust-v0.151.0), [commit](https://github.com/openai/codex/commit/78c290807ce710180111df227df3b7a4fe845452).
- Installed help accepts `codex resume [SESSION_ID] [PROMPT]`. Current [official CLI reference](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/developer-commands?surface=cli) documents resume as stable, but does not guarantee multi-client propagation, draft safety, serialization, ownership, or frontend lifetime.
- A standalone resume launches another embedded app-server. If the target TUI is live, the writer lock rejects it with `thread ... already has an active writer`; it does not attach to the existing logical core. This is enforced by [writer_lock.rs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openai/codex/rust-v0.151.0/codex-rs/thread-store/src/local/writer_lock.rs).
- Multiple clients can share a live thread only when connected to the same app-server endpoint. Warm resume reuses live conversation state, subscribes the connection, and broadcasts events to subscribers. [thread_lifecycle.rs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openai/codex/rust-v0.151.0/codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/thread_lifecycle.rs).
- `codex queue` performs provider-free durable enqueueing through `thread/queue/add`; starting is separate and rejects active/pending turns. [queue source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openai/codex/rust-v0.151.0/codex-rs/tui/src/session_queue_commands.rs), [queue processor](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openai/codex/rust-v0.151.0/codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/thread_queue_processor.rs).

Controlled disposable session `01a05d02-ed17-77c1-ac50-9118b6e991e5` proved:

- Simple and multiline synthetic drafts remained intact after rejected second resumes.
- Two near-simultaneous resumes against an empty-composer live TUI both exited 1 with the active-writer conflict.
- Queueing during an active turn succeeded without changing the rollout or starting a provider turn.
- Two simultaneous queue additions serialized, but arrival order was nondeterministic.
- Identical prompts created distinct queue records: text or `clientUserMessageId` is not an idempotency barrier.
- Closing the embedded frontend released the writer; a later cold resume succeeded.
- A nonexistent UUID exited 1 with “No saved session found.”
- CWD can be overridden and is therefore not a session-identity fence.
- Provider completions, exact human-Enter/remote-start ordering, deleted/corrupt rollouts, and crash-stale-lock recovery remain unproven because network access was denied or destructive testing was unnecessary. Treat them as unsafe.

The operator experiment remains valid positive evidence only for its observed Desktop condition: session `01a05a17-c5c5-7463-8670-14c5127f2072` durably records `test` at `12:23:40.954Z` and `Received.` at `12:23:46.150Z` while the original frontend continued. It does not prove arbitrary standalone CLI attachment.

Safe implementation contract:

- Migrate under separate authority to one writer-owning persistent app-server endpoint; all clients must use `--remote`.
- Dispatch directly with `thread/queue/add`, not `codex resume ... MESSAGE`.
- Use a durable CAS activation lease bound to supervisor ID, generation, session ID, dispatcher owner, PID/start ticks, and expiry.
- Maintain an external unique event ledger. Use tiny messages such as `OPSLE_WAKE v1 event=<uuid> gen=<n>`.
- Queue while busy; call `thread/queue/start` only for the leased head event when idle.
- Mark stale-generation, terminal-task, and historical requests obsolete without rewriting or delivering them.
- After
